title: Finite return-square cancellation of absolute Frobenius
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $q=p^a$ and $k$ the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and put $g=g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Use the derived pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the point functor $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Fix $m\geq1$ and $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, and let $z:s\to X$ be its induced geometric point. Write $\Phi$ for the $q$-power scheme Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], $H=\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_X$ and $r=\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_s=g_s^{-m}$ for absolute Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Then $\Phi^mz=z$, $Hz=zr$ and $g^mz=zg_s^m$ as scheme maps.

Put $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ with $n\geq1$, $P=Lz_\Lambda^*$, $U=Lg_{s,\Lambda}^*$, $G=Lg_\Lambda^*$ and $J=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}P$. Define $I_N^{(0)}=1$ and $I_N^{(j+1)}=\iota_{U^jN}I_N^{(j)}$ from the specified point transport [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Let $v_K:U^mPK\xrightarrow{\sim}PG^mK$ be the pullback-composition comparison for $g^mz=zg_s^m$, using the canonical composition maps [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Let $\rho_K:JK\to JL(\Phi^m)^*K$ be the comparison for $\Phi^mz=z$. Let $\tau_X:L H^*\xrightarrow{\sim}1$ and $\tau_s:Lr^*\xrightarrow{\sim}1$ be exactly the absolute-Frobenius trivializations [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] at exponent $am$. Specify $\kappa_K^{(m)}=(\tau_X)_{L(g^m)^*K}\,c_{H,g^m,K}$, the canonical multiplicative comparison [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]. Identify $L(g^m)^*$ with $G^m$ by the canonical compositors.

For every sheaf $N$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the final-object formula for $\tau_{s,L(g_s^m)^*N}$, under $Lr^*L(g_s^m)^*N\cong N$, is the restriction map $\operatorname{res}_{g_s^m}:N(s,1)\to N(s,g_s^m)$, namely the inverse of restriction along $r$. This is the $m$-fold successive point transport under the same compositor. For every complex $K$ whose class is in the finite constructible category [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], one has
$$J(\kappa_K^{(m)})\rho_K=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(v_K)I_{PK}^{(m)}.$$
This is already an equality of the specified chain maps on flat-term K-flat representatives before derived localization, using restriction, inverse-image colimit insertion, coefficient identification and the relative-Frobenius trivialization; it includes the canonical composition identifications on both paths. The normalization contains no scalar rescaling.

proof.text: Write $h=g_s^m$, $f=g^m$ and $T=L f^*$. On an affine chart through the image of $y$, write its evaluation as $e:A_0\to\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$. Then $z^\sharp(a\otimes b)=e(a)b$. The maps for $\Phi^mz$, $Hz$ and $f z$ send $a\otimes b$ respectively to $e(a)^{q^m}b=e(a)b$, to $e(a)^{q^m}b^{q^m}=e(a)b^{q^m}$, and to $e(a)\gamma^m(b)=\gamma^m(e(a)b)$. These are the maps for $z,zr,zh$. Absolute Frobenius and its iterates commute with every scheme map because homomorphisms preserve powers. The inverse convention $\gamma(b)^q=b$ gives $rh=hr=1$. The factorization cited below gives $\Phi^m=fH$. These computations concern scheme maps, including the structure-sheaf maps, and therefore glue from affine charts.

proof.text: Use the automorphism inverse-image formula to identify $(h^*N)(U,u)$ with $N(U,hu)$, after transporting the constant coefficient action. Its normalization in the colimit model is explicit: the index $V=(U,hu)$ with the graph $U\to s\times_{s,h}V$ is initial in $\mathcal I_U$, since an index $(V',\theta)$ gives exactly the map $U\to V'$ obtained by its second projection. It is terminal in $\mathcal I_U^{\mathrm{op}}$, so insertion at it is the evaluation identification; the resulting presheaf is already a sheaf. For module pullback the coefficient isomorphism sends $x\otimes a$ to $a x$, with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Consequently this identification uses exactly the insertion and coefficient map in point transport, not a chosen isomorphism of fibers.

proof.text: For successive automorphisms $h_1,h_2$ of $s$, the reindexed sheaf has value $N(U,h_2h_1u)$. On the colimit insertions the ordinary pullback compositor takes the graph for the composite to its two successive graphs; both have second projection the same map to the original site object. Its tensor map takes $x\otimes a$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes a$. Thus the canonical compositor identifies the successive reindexings with reindexing by the composite, including coefficient action; constants compose by [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition]. In particular the identity reindexing is the canonical identity-pullback identification. These are the termwise representatives of the derived compositors specified in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

proof.text: Compute the normalization of $\tau_s$ for an arbitrary module sheaf $M$. The trivialization in [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] is adjoint to the direct-image map $\delta_M:M\to r_*M$ given by inverse restriction along relative Frobenius. Evaluate the adjoint unit equation of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] at the object $V=(s,r)$ of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The object $B_rV$ has both projections equal to the identity under its identification with $(s,1)$, since $r$ is an automorphism. Relative Frobenius $V\to B_rV$ is then the underlying map $r$, so $\delta_M(V)$ is restriction along $r^{-1}:(s,1)\to(s,r)$. The inverse-image unit at $V$ is the identity in the reindexing model of Step 2. The unit equation therefore says precisely that $\tau_{s,M}(s,1):M(s,r)\to M(s,1)$ is $\operatorname{res}_{r^{-1}}$. This derives its direction from the specified adjunction normalization.

proof.text: Apply Step 4 to $M=h^*N$. Reindexing gives $M(s,r)=N(s,hr)=N(s,1)$ and $M(s,1)=N(s,h)$. Restriction along $r^{-1}$ becomes restriction along the arrow $h:(s,h)\to(s,1)$ for $N$. Hence $\tau_{s,h^*N}$, preceded by the canonical $N\cong r^*h^*N$, is exactly $\operatorname{res}_h$ under Step 2. This proves the requested sheaf formula for every $N$, without a constructibility or flatness condition.

proof.text: Under Step 2, the definition [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] sends a section to its restriction along $g_s$, since its subsequent insertion is the reindexing identification and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ is the coefficient identification. Induct on $j$ for the asserted formula for $I_N^{(j)}$. For $j=0$ it is identity. If it is restriction from $N(s,1)$ to $N(s,g_s^j)$, the next transport on $(g_s^*)^jN$ is restriction along $g_s:(s,g_s^{j+1})\to(s,g_s^j)$. Presheaf functoriality makes the composite restriction along $g_s^{j+1}$. Step 3 supplies exactly the canonical compositor used in this induction. Taking $j=m$ identifies Step 5 with $I_N^{(m)}$.

proof.text:
For the remaining comparison keep $P=Lz^*$, and write $R=Lr^*$, $V=Lh^*$ and $S=LH^*$. Let $c_{u,v}:L(vu)^*\to Lu^*Lv^*$ denote the specified compositor. Define $d_K=c_{r,z,TK}c_{z,H,TK}^{-1}:PSTK\to RPTK$, using $Hz=zr$, and $e_N=c_{r,h,N}:N\to RVN$, using $hr=1$. Let $v_K:VPK\to PTK$ be the return comparison of the item. Let $b_K:PK\to PL(\Phi^m)^*K$ be the pullback-composition map for $\Phi^m z=z$, so that $\rho_K=\Gamma(s,b_K)$. Put $a_K=P(c_{H,f,K})b_K:PK\to PSTK$. Associativity of the canonical compositors gives
$$d_K a_K=R(v_K)e_{PK}:PK\longrightarrow RPTK.$$
Indeed, the left side composes the comparisons for the factorization $fHz=z$ through $H z=z r$; the right side composes them through $f z=z h$ and $hr=1$. The triple-composition identity of [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence], applied to these factorizations, identifies both with the comparison for the same composite $fHz=z$, followed by $c_{r,z,TK}$. The termwise maps have the same nested colimit indices and send $x\otimes a$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes a$, so this identity also holds on those representatives.

proof.text: Apply the arbitrary-pullback naturality equation of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] to $z:s\to X$, exponent $am$, and input $TK$. With $d$ as above it reads $P(\tau_{X,TK})=\tau_{s,PTK}d_K$. Naturality of $\tau_s$ in the morphism $v_K:VPK\to PTK$ reads $\tau_{s,PTK}R(v_K)=v_K\tau_{s,VPK}$. The finite coefficient ring and characteristic-$p$ schemes satisfy exactly the hypotheses of that node; its naturality permits the geometric point $z$ without an additional smoothness or etaleness hypothesis.

proof.text:
Substitute the prescribed $\kappa_K^{(m)}=\tau_{X,TK}c_{H,f,K}$. Steps 7 and 8 yield
$$P(\kappa_K^{(m)})b_K=\tau_{s,PTK}d_K a_K=\tau_{s,PTK}R(v_K)e_{PK}=v_K\tau_{s,VPK}e_{PK}.$$
Apply $\Gamma(s,-)$. By Steps 5 and 6 the last two factors become $I_{PK}^{(m)}$. Since $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}$ is exactly termwise $\Gamma(s,-)$ at finite level, the result is
$$J(\kappa_K^{(m)})\rho_K=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(v_K)I_{PK}^{(m)}.$$
The identification $T=G^m$ is the iterated compositor, so Step 3 and the triple associativity identity also give the requested iterate convention.

proof.text: All maps in Steps 2–6 are maps of module sheaves natural in $N$, hence apply degreewise to arbitrary complexes and commute with their differentials. The naturality in Step 8 comes from equality of relative-Frobenius maps under base change: their first projections are the absolute powers and their second projections the structure maps; thus it is an equality of the specified ordinary module maps before applying the exact termwise derived construction. Step 7 was checked with the normalized termwise compositors. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; iterated pullbacks remain flat-term K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. Exactness of finite constant-coefficient pullback and of point sections allows these maps and equalities to descend through localization, using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Thus the displayed identity is already the specified chain-map identity on these representatives. Every coefficient comparison preserves $1$ and every remaining operation is restriction or colimit insertion; no scalar has been introduced. The argument applies to all complexes, hence in particular to the stated bounded constructible objects.
